coachingPoints: Script your top 3 after-timeout plays and practice them under simulated pressure.
Decide your up-3 foul philosophy before the season, not in the moment.
Practice free throws with consequences to simulate late-game pressure.
Debrief every close game: evaluate which decisions were right, regardless of the outcome.
commonMistakes: Fouling a jump shooter while ahead late in the game.
Using all timeouts too early and having none left for the final possession.
Forcing a contested three when a quick two was available.
Panicking and abandoning the offense entirely in the last minute.
description: How to think in the final two minutes — foul strategy, ATO plays, timeout usage, and staying composed when the game is on the line.
gameSituations: Tie game, 15 seconds left, one timeout: holding for the final shot.
Up 3 with 8 seconds left: the foul-or-defend decision.
Down 2 with 20 seconds: quick two and foul, or play for the three.

howTo.detail: Before the final two minutes, confirm the full picture: score, team fouls, timeouts, bonus situation. Every late-game decision flows from these facts.
howTo.title: Know your scenario

howTo.detail: Decide in advance whether you foul to prevent the tying three or trust your defense — and communicate it clearly so all five players execute the same plan.
howTo.title: Up 3, late: have a foul philosophy

howTo.detail: Know the math cold. A fast two preserves time for another possession; a three ties it immediately. Make this decision before the possession starts, not during it.
howTo.title: Down late: quick two vs. three

howTo.detail: Save at least one timeout for the final possession. Know your sideline and baseline after-timeout plays — the ones you have actually practiced.
howTo.title: Use timeouts to advance and organize

howTo.detail: The last shot should come from your most reliable creator and decision-maker — not necessarily your best shooter. Trust the player who makes the right read under pressure.
howTo.title: Get the ball to your best decision-maker

howTo.detail: Slow your breathing, stick to the plan, and make the simple play. Panic creates turnovers; composure creates good shots. The team takes its emotional cue from its leaders.
howTo.title: Stay composed

title: End-of-Game Decisions
whatIsIt: End-of-game decisions are the choices made in the final minutes when every possession can decide the outcome: whether to foul when up three, when to use timeouts, which play to run out of a timeout, who takes the last shot. The game slows down, the pressure rises, and thinking clearly becomes a skill of its own.

Great closers prepare for these moments long before they arrive. They know the scenarios — up 3, down 2, tie game — and already have a plan for each. Composure is not the absence of pressure; it is having a decision already made before the pressure arrives.
whyItMatters: Players remember who made the last shot, but games are usually decided by the five small decisions before it. Teams with a clear late-game plan win more close games regardless of talent. This is where coaching and basketball IQ matter most.
It is also where preparation compounds. A team that has rehearsed its late-game scenarios plays free; a team improvising plays tight. The work done in October wins the game in March.
